clue.text: Annoyed old boy returning to that place died

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation for old boy is read backwards

parts.note: OB is the standard abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
to that place means there
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone irritated that a former schoolmate went back to some place and died there.
explanation.definitionFit: Bothered is a synonym of annoyed: irritated or put out.

clue.text: Eastern female entertained by tedious person earlier

indicators.note: entertained by means hosted inside, so the two letters sit within the word for a tedious person

parts.note: a bore is a tedious person

explanation.surface: A woman from the East had once been stuck with a dull host.
explanation.definitionFit: Before and earlier are synonyms meaning at a previous time.

clue.text: Bird in this grass-like plant is escaping

indicators.note: escaping means the two letters of the clue word is get away from the word this

parts.note: a rush is a grass-like marsh plant

explanation.surface: A bird caught in the reeds is trying to get away.
explanation.definitionFit: The thrush is a songbird, such as the song thrush or mistle thrush.

clue.text: Did well, no longer having prison-style accommodation?

parts.note: ex means former, no longer something
celled describes being housed in cells, like a prison

explanation.surface: A former inmate who made good once out of jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second half is a whimsical reading of the word split in two.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to perform outstandingly, so excelled means did very well.

clue.text: Characters at the edges of empire reported peace

indicators.note: reported signals that the letters are heard spoken, as the plural of the letter name
characters at the edges of take the first and last letters of the next word

explanation.surface: News arrives from the frontier provinces that peace has broken out.
explanation.walkthrough: The two edge letters of 'empire' are both E, and two Es said aloud sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease means calm or freedom from worry, so peace in the sense of tranquillity.

clue.text: Fight doctor wearing his white garment?

indicators.note: the doctor is wearing the garment, so it goes inside the word for that garment

parts.note: a doctor's white garment is his white coat
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor squaring up for a brawl while still in his white lab coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat and fight are synonyms, as nouns or verbs: armed struggle or conflict.

clue.text: Animals to rest after swimming

indicators.note: after swimming suggests the letters of to rest moving about freely into a new order

explanation.surface: Creatures settling down for a nap after a long swim.
explanation.definitionFit: Otters are semi-aquatic mammals of rivers and coasts.

clue.text: Those that mix in British libraries?

parts.note: libraries lend books, so they are lenders

explanation.surface: Readers who socialise in the public libraries of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Blenders are kitchen machines that mix ingredients together.

clue.text: Storms encountered going north — things that bother you

indicators.note: going north in a down clue means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: met means encountered
pests are nuisances, things that bother you

explanation.surface: Bad weather met heading north, along with irritating insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempests are violent storms with strong winds.

clue.text: Supporting English actors, making prediction

parts.note: to be for something is to support it
the cast of a play is its set of actors

explanation.surface: Backing the English performers to win, a pundit makes a prediction.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecast is a prediction of future events, such as the weather.

clue.text: Course of godly soul getting about in the morning

parts.note: a saint is a godly soul, abbreviated ST
RE means about or concerning, as in letter headings
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: A holy person rising early and moving about, describing the course of their day.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream is a watercourse, the course of a flowing brook or river.

clue.text: Lines penned by directors offering a post

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed, so the lines sit inside the directors

parts.note: a company's directors make up its board
L is the abbreviation for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: A letter written by the board offering someone a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' reads as a job; here it is a short thick upright pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A bollard is a short sturdy post, for mooring boats or blocking traffic.

clue.text: Sound in street restricted by regulation

indicators.note: restricted by means held inside, so the street abbreviation sits within the word for regulation

parts.note: a rule is a regulation

explanation.surface: A noise heard in a street where traffic rules limit access.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustle is a soft crackling sound, such as leaves or paper moving.

clue.text: Quiet men line up for traditional prison food

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men
a ridge is a raised line, a line standing up from a surface

explanation.surface: Silent inmates queue for their old-fashioned jail breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge is also British slang for a prison sentence, which the definition plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Oat gruel was the classic breakfast served in British jails, hence the slang for doing time.

clue.text: Showing dignity, this person's stifling a joke

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so the word for this person's wraps round the rest

parts.note: this person's, from the setter's view, is my
a jest is a joke

explanation.surface: Someone keeping a straight face by suppressing a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Majesty means stately grandeur, an impressive dignity of bearing.

clue.text: Archdeacon attached to friend in a corrupt fashion

parts.note: an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A senior cleric teaming up with a crony to do something shady.
explanation.definitionFit: Venal means open to bribery, so acting venally is behaving corruptly.

clue.text: Ornament to corrode

definitions.meaning: a decorative pattern of interlaced lines, as in fretwork
to ... is to wear away or eat into, as water ... stone

explanation.surface: A decoration about to rust away.
explanation.definitionFit: Fret has both senses: a geometric decorative band, and to gnaw or erode.

clue.text: Feature of restaurant that could be drab, alas

indicators.note: that could be signals the following letters can be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A restaurant's self-service counter that might, sadly, be dull.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad bar is a counter in a restaurant where diners help themselves to salads.

clue.text: Feature of foyer with tiles?

parts.note: tiles is slang for hats, so a hallway fixture holding them is meant, not a tiled floor

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiles' suggests flooring; it is old slang for hats.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand with pegs in an entrance hall where coats and headgear are hung.

clue.text: Requiring, by the sound of it, the action of a masseur

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word for requiring is heard, not written

parts.note: needing means requiring

explanation.surface: Needing, apparently, what a massage therapist does.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneading is working muscles with the hands, pressing and squeezing as a masseur does.

clue.text: Just out of bed, we hear, and off

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for the first phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: an anchor is aweigh when it has just been lifted clear of the seabed

explanation.surface: Someone barely up who has already left the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is the seabed, not a sleeper's bed: a nautical term.
explanation.definitionFit: Away and off are synonyms meaning gone or absent, as in 'off on holiday'.

clue.text: In a circle you and I will lead

indicators.note: will lead puts the pair of pronouns at the front of what follows

parts.note: you and I together are we
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: A circle dance where the two of us will take the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a hat is to be wearing one, so the preposition matches the participle.

clue.text: More than one little bird flinches

definitions.meaning: small plump game birds, here in the plural
to quail is to shrink back or cower in fear

explanation.surface: Several small birds draw back in fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Quail is both a small game bird and a verb meaning to recoil in fear.

clue.text: Good US soldier turning up in pub in Scottish town

indicators.note: in places the reversed pair inside the word for pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means reading upwards, so good and soldier are reversed

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An American serviceman upended in a bar in a Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Biggar is a small market town in South Lanarkshire, Scotland.

clue.text: Quarrel after cheat turns up to use bank facility?

indicators.note: after places the quarrel word behind the reversed cheat
turns up in a down clue means the word for cheat reads upwards, reversed

parts.note: to rob is to cheat someone of something
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: An argument after a swindle comes to light, then a trip to the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a loan is the bank facility; to borrow is to take money on loan.

clue.text: Attacks made by idiot with a lust out of control

parts.note: an ass is a fool or idiot

indicators.note: out of control signals the letters of a lust running wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Assaults committed by a fool whose desire has got out of hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Assaults are violent attacks, as nouns or verbs.

clue.text: A coin's tossed in a place for gambling

indicators.note: a coin tossed is flipped about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A coin flipped at a gaming venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is a building where people gamble at roulette, cards and similar games.

clue.text: Word of warning in underground venue

definitions.meaning: Latin for beware, used by British schoolboys as a lookout's warning
a hollow chamber in rock below ground

explanation.surface: A warning spoken in an underground club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep cave' was British public-school slang for keeping watch for teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cave is Latin for beware, and also a natural hollow under the earth.

clue.text: Support needed by Elizabeth, contrary nut

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

indicators.note: contrary means going the opposite way, so the short form of the name is read backwards

parts.note: Liz is a short form of Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Elizabeth, a stubborn crank, needing support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrary nut' looks like an awkward person; 'contrary' is the reversal signal and 'nut' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazil is a large three-sided nut from South America.

clue.text: Writer and performer entertaining old crooner?

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the crooner's name goes inside the performer

parts.note: a singer is a performer
Al Bowlly and Al Jolson were famous old-time crooners, giving AL

explanation.surface: An author and an entertainer playing host to a veteran ballad singer.
explanation.definitionFit: J. D. Salinger was the American novelist who wrote The Catcher in the Rye.

clue.text: Component of 17 right to put on a plate?

parts.note: a dish is a plate

explanation.surface: Something from the buffet that would be right to serve up.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is SALAD BAR, so a component of it is a salad vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A radish is a crisp red root vegetable commonly found in salads.

clue.text: One may have several shrubs — how to handle garden tool?

indicators.note: to handle means to hold, so the little word encloses the tool

parts.note: an edger is a garden tool for trimming lawn edges

explanation.surface: A gardener asking how to operate a new piece of kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedgerow is a line of bushes along a field edge, made up of many shrubs.
